pages.title: What Lives Up Here
pages.text: Most of what lives on a Charter fragment is recognisable. Pigs, sheep, cows, chickens — Charter survey ships seed them in the first year. Wolves and foxes arrive on their own, eventually, by some sky-walked route nobody has charted.$(br2)Past the seeding, the wild fills in.

pages.title: Useful Drops
pages.text: $(l)Sheep$() — wool, mutton. The Foreman's first textile.$(br2)$(l)Cow$() — leather, beef. The Foreman's first armour binding.$(br2)$(l)Chicken$() — feathers for arrows, eggs for the Federation breakfast docket.$(br2)$(l)Bee$() — honey, wax. The wax matters. Charter dockets need wax.

pages.title: Dangerous Flora
pages.text: The Charter's surveys note that the fragment's lower terraces sometimes host $(o)source-touched$() plant life — flowers that move on their own, vines that grow toward a forge fire.$(br2)Reformers find them useful. Traditionalists burn them. The Charter has signed both responses depending on the auditor.
